catalog_citation: Innes, Gordon (1966). An Introduction to Grebo. London: School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London (printed by Mouton, The Hague). Carried via the StressTyp2 entry(source 684); corroborating snippets from Google Books volume T-AtAAAAMAAJ…
catalog_quote: [StressTyp2 passage 1013, citing Innes (1966:19)] Stress in Grebo is a complex of phonetic features, some of which are very difficult to describe precisely, but others, such as lengthening of consonants, are more readily described. Two degrees of stress are rcognised, 'strong' (maximal) stress, and 'zero' stress. Words can be differentiated only by the place of the stress. There are three styles of pronunciation: Unemphatic and Emphatic 1 and 2. ... [Google Books snippets, Innes 1966 pp.18-19] There is an important characteristic of Grebo speech which can conveniently be called stress. ... Unemphatic Pronunciation (UP), Emphatic Pronunciation 1 (EP1), and ... stressed also in EP1, but is front-stressed in EP2. All disyllabic nouns and verbs bear one strong stress, and most of the former occur with all three styles of pronunciation ... [Google Books snippet, van der Hulst et al. 2010 Survey, Gr…

audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: the the StressTyp2 entrytext and its source row 684 (= Innes 1966) are verbatim in the held SQL dump, and every Innes 1966 / Survey 2010 snippet fragment in the record is verbatim in the copies we hold; but Innes 1966 pp.18-19 themselves are not yet obtained (Rosetta excerpts stop at p.15), so the check is against the carrier, hence partly confirmed. (2) Deciding source: effectively StressTyp2 quoting Innes 1966, a SOAS descriptive grammar that is the fullest description of the language and the only Glottolog 'grammar'; Berry & Innes 1957 (snippet downloaded now) gives the same two-degree, three-style stress analysis, and a 1975 MSU working paper reuses it as a 'stress reversing rule'. Languoid identity checks out (Berry & Innes place their Grebo on the Fishtown-Cavalla coast = Glebo, Southern Grebo), even though StressTyp2 filed the lect under grv. (3) New finding: Newman 1986, the onl
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again.— I re-opened every held piece and the other first reader's finding stands. (1) StressTyp2 dump line 28753: row (1013, 684, NULL, 'Stress in Grebo is a complex of phonetic features.. Two degrees of stress are rcognised, strong (maximal) stress, and zero stress. Words can be differentiated only by the place of the stress. There are three styles of pronunciation: Unemphatic and Emphatic 1 and 2 (see remarks). Innes (1966:19).'; line 50489: source 684 = 'Innes, Gordon (1966). An introduction to Grebo. London: SOAS'. Verbatim match to the record's quote (typo 'rcognised' is StressTyp2's).
